title: The Three Little Pigs
retold: An original gentle retelling of the traditional public-domain tale for ages 4 to 6. All three pigs stay safe; the wolf gives up and runs away.

text: Once upon a time, three little pigs set off to build their own homes.
"Let us build strong houses!" said the third little pig.
The first little pig built a house of straw.
"All done! Now I can play!" he cheered.
The second little pig built a house of sticks.
Tap, tap, tap! Soon his house was ready.
The third little pig worked hard with bricks.
He built strong walls and a sturdy door.
Then a hungry wolf came to the straw house.
"Little pig, little pig, let me come in!" he called.
"Not by the hair on my chinny chin chin!" cried the pig.
"Then I will huff, and I will puff, and I will blow your house down!" growled the wolf.
Whoosh! The straw flew everywhere!
The first pig ran to the house of sticks.
The wolf followed them to the stick house.
He huffed and puffed. Crack! Down fell the sticks!
"Run!" cried the pigs. They raced to the brick house.
The third pig opened the door.
"Quick! Come inside!" he cried.
All three pigs shut the sturdy door together.
The wolf huffed. He puffed. He puffed again!
But the brick house did not move.
"Our strong house will keep us safe!" said the third pig.
The tired wolf gave up and ran away.
The three little pigs cheered and hugged.
"Next time, we will build carefully and help each other!" they said.
The pigs shared a warm supper in their strong brick house.
They were safe, happy, and together.
The End.
